title: Fixed Cutaway Bobbin Grip and Blunt Eye Awl
description: One newly authored complete hand-sewing-awl-style static cutaway exterior. One thick bulged palm-grip shell has a deliberate wide side cutaway exposing its complete axial bobbin, retaining spindle and one whole wound-thread appearance. A proud rear cap and a complete front tapered ferrule retain the shell; a separate short collet-shaped nose carries one finite blunt needle-like stem with a genuinely open short eye at its end. One continuous short thread appearance leads from the internal spool toward the front guide. Unlike the old side-gear drill there is no open C drive frame, side wheel, crank or rotating gear train; unlike the long-horn sewing machine there is no table, lower horn, overhead head or external thread stand. The whole internal bobbin and hand-shell organization is newly authored, not an extracted old needle or handgrip. Three opaque PBR roles, metres Z up and centred ground origin, one model zero scenes. Deliberate cutaway, not an intact usable tool. Static art only: no stitching, needle penetration, sharp cutting edge, thread tension or path validation, chuck fit, handling, manufacture or safety capability. Rigging animation interaction not made.
